comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete manifest selectors covering 130 BDDL definitions and 5 benchmark/predicate Python files. All 135 indexed local files exist and match their recorded SHA-256 hashes. Scanned the complete definition-name/language inventory, then read the closest stove task and its complete Turnon predicate mapping.
comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates a gripper opening stop to 90°, locks the coupled screw/jam nut without disturbing the setting, and verifies retained articulation; LIBERO's closest task only turns on a stove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver and wrench seating, bimanual countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and repeated articulated verification. LIBERO requires a single control actuation represented by Turnon.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ±3° retained opening, seated/retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, ≤2° drift, and hands-off clearance. LIBERO requires only the stove's boolean turn_on() predicate.

closest_tasks.name: turn_on_the_stove
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Actuate the stove control sufficiently to enter its on state.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The Turnon predicate is true; its registered implementation delegates to arg.turn_on().
closest_tasks.reason: It shares rotary actuation but has no adjustable stop, threaded lock, counterholding, drift preservation, or released-cycle verification.

comparisons.reason: The complete LIBERO inventory contains articulated opening and stove-control tasks, but none tests locking a calibrated screw setting against jam-nut reaction and verifying retained motion.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete kitchen selectors and all 381 indexed Python definitions/registry files; every local path exists and matches its recorded SHA-256. Scanned the full class/docstring inventory and read the complete kitchen_stove.py definition containing the closest intermediate-angle task.
comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and mechanically locks a gripper's maximum opening, then tests retention; RoboCasa LowerHeat moves a stove knob from high into a low-heat interval.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both regulate an articulated angular control, but only the candidate requires concentric two-tool screw/nut engagement and bimanual countertorque that preserves the adjustment during locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained 90° opening, nut seating/retention, three cycles, drift, and release clearance. LowerHeat succeeds whenever the absolute stove-knob value lies in its low-heat interval.

closest_tasks.name: LowerHeat
closest_tasks.objective: Lower the heat of a kettle by adjusting its stove burner knob.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Rotate one stove knob into a permitted angular/state interval.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The target knob's absolute value is between 0.35 and STOVE_HIGH_MIN minus 0.00000001.
closest_tasks.reason: Intermediate angular regulation overlaps, but LowerHeat does not lock the setting, resist coupled fastener reaction, use two concentric tools, or demonstrate hands-off retention through cycles.

comparisons.reason: LowerHeat is the closest goal-level neighbor, yet the candidate's central tested ability is mechanically preserving and locking a calibrated stop under countertorque, not merely selecting an angular range.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both repository components and all 11 indexed environment/registry Python files against their recorded hashes. Scanned the complete environment inventory and read the full closest articulated-joint implementation, including reset, instruction, and evaluation logic.
comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates, locks, and functionally verifies an angular gripper stop; SimplerEnv opens a selected cabinet drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires precision tool seating and coordinated countertorque followed by repeated jaw actuation. SimplerEnv requires grasping/pulling one prismatic articulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle, locked hardware, repeated cycles, drift limits, and clearance. OpenDrawer succeeds when drawer qpos reaches at least 0.15.

closest_tasks.name: OpenDrawerInSceneEnv
closest_tasks.objective: Open the selected top, middle, or bottom drawer.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Pull a frictional prismatic drawer joint.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The target drawer joint position is at least 0.15.
closest_tasks.reason: It shares articulated motion only; it lacks fastener adjustment, locking reaction, setting preservation, tools, and post-lock cycle retention.

comparisons.reason: No SimplerEnv definition tests threaded adjustment or bimanual locknut counterholding; its closest articulation task is a single-joint drawer displacement.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both recorded BEHAVIOR/BDDL components: 1,119 BDDL files and 3 backend Python files, all 1,122 indexed paths present with matching hashes. Scanned the complete activity inventory, read the furniture and camera-attachment definitions, and read the complete AttachedTo backend to resolve the abstract attached predicate.
comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an adjustable robot-gripper stop and validates retained function. BEHAVIOR's closest assembly goals attach components or a camera to a supporting structure.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires actual driver/wrench seating and countertorque on a coupled screw/jam nut. BEHAVIOR AttachedTo aligns male/female metadata frames after contact and creates a fixed or spherical joint; it does not encode screw tightening or calibration preservation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires quantitative retained angle, nut retention, three functional cycles, drift, and clearance. BEHAVIOR attachment tasks require AttachedTo relationships between named objects.

closest_tasks.name: attach_a_camera_to_a_tripod
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a digital camera to a camera tripod.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Bring compatible attachment metadata frames into contact and alignment so the backend creates an attachment joint.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The camera's AttachedTo state names the tripod as its parent.
closest_tasks.reason: A real tripod may use a screw, but this benchmark definition/backend tests generic contact-triggered attachment, not threaded engagement, counterholding, calibrated locking, or retained articulation.

closest_tasks.name: assembling_furniture
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a desk bracket to a top and four legs to the bracket.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align and attach several rigid furniture components through the generic AttachedTo mechanism.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The bracket is attached to the top and every desk leg is attached to the bracket.
closest_tasks.reason: It is multi-component assembly, but its generic attachment predicates do not test adjustment to a numeric setting, locknut reaction, or functional retention cycles.

comparisons.reason: Inspecting the backend resolves the apparent assembly overlap: BEHAVIOR's relevant goals create generic metadata-frame attachment joints rather than measuring the candidate's coupled fastener calibration-and-locking ability.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both complete official JSON files against manifest hashes, covering all 10 published Tier-1 setup/rubric records and 14 linked industrial procedures. Scanned every task and procedure mapping, then read the full DC-knob record and its linked proc-micropod procedure.
comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then verifies retention. DC-knob rotates a marked dimmer knob to a fixed visual mark as a proxy for a UPS rotary bypass operation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require angular alignment to a target. Candidate additionally requires two-tool coaxial seating, countertorque against locknut reaction, regrasping, withdrawal, and repeated articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ±3° locked retention, three cycles, ≤2° drift, retained nuts, and one-second clearance. DC-knob gives full credit when the knob line points at the goal mark and partial credit for noticeable clockwise progress.

closest_tasks.name: DC-knob — Turn the knob to the mark
closest_tasks.quote: The line on the knob points at the goal mark (turned clockwise to it).
closest_tasks.objective: Turn a rotary dimmer knob clockwise until its line aligns with the marked goal.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Single-hand rotary control and visual angular alignment.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Full credit at the goal mark, half credit for noticeable clockwise motion short of it, and zero for no clockwise motion.
closest_tasks.reason: The angular target is a meaningful overlap, but DC-knob has no coupled adjustment screw, jam-nut locking, counterholding, drift constraint, or functional-cycle retention.

closest_tasks.name: proc-micropod — Put a UPS on maintenance bypass with a rotary switch
closest_tasks.quote: Transfer the rotary switch from UPS to MAINS, provided the MAINS lamp is illuminated
closest_tasks.objective: Transfer a UPS maintenance-bypass rotary switch from UPS to MAINS.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Rotate a selector after checking the enabling indicator.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The procedure reaches the MAINS selector state before subsequent shutdown and disconnection steps.
closest_tasks.reason: This industrial procedure supports DC-knob's selector-turning ability but does not include mechanical calibration, locknut countertorque, or post-lock repeatability testing.

comparisons.reason: DataCenterBench contains the strongest target-angle analogue, but its tested outcome is direct selector alignment rather than preserving and locking an adjustable stop under coupled fastener reaction.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete task/config selectors: 55 Python files and 55 YAML files, all 110 indexed paths present with matching SHA-256 hashes. Checked the dynamic task registry and scanned the complete paired inventory, then read the full fasten_screws task implementation and YAML specification.
comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts one screw-defined stop, locks the setting with a jam nut, and validates retained gripper motion. RoboDojo fasten_screws inserts and tightens three color-matched nuts and bolts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve threaded hardware and tightening. Candidate's essential skill is bimanual counterholding of concentric tools so jam-nut torque does not disturb a calibrated stop; RoboDojo checks insertion/alignment/depth of three independent fasteners.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening, lock seating, repeat cycles, drift limits, and release clearance. RoboDojo scores one, two, or three fasteners by upright axis, ≤0.001 XY mismatch, ≥0.009 insertion depth, and open grippers.

closest_tasks.name: fasten_screws
closest_tasks.quote: Insert and tighten each screw into the nut of the same color.
closest_tasks.objective: Insert and tighten each of three screws into the color-matched nut.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align and seat three independent threaded nut/bolt pairs.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Each credited pair is upright, within 0.001 XY distance, and inserted to the 0.009 depth threshold; grippers must be open.
closest_tasks.reason: This is the closest hardware-level neighbor, but it does not preserve a calibrated setting while tightening a coupled jam nut or verify hands-off retained articulation afterward.

comparisons.reason: Shared tightening is not the candidate's central tested ability: RoboDojo measures independent fastener insertion/depth, while the candidate measures countertorque-preserved calibration, locking, and functional retention.
